title: The Skip-Level Promotion Approval Chain
scenario_text:
You're reviewing Q2 promotion packets before the calibration meeting next week. One promotion stands out: Marcus Thompson, Senior Product Manager → Director of Product, two levels up. The packet shows he'd be reporting directly to VP Product Jamie Ross, skipping the Group PM layer entirely.

The formal approval chain per the People Ops policy (updated January 2026) requires: (1) Manager recommendation, (2) VP approval, (3) CEO approval for skip-level promos, and (4) Compensation Committee review for any Director+ promotion creating >$180K base. Marcus's proposed comp is $195K base.

The promotion packet in Asana shows: Manager (Jamie Ross) recommended 6/15, VP approved 6/15 (same person), CEO approval field shows "Verbal OK - 6/18 ELT meeting per Jamie." The packet notes reference "Discussed in Q2 OKR review, Marcus taking on platform strategy ownership post-reorg."

You weren't at the June 18 ELT meeting (you were in back-to-back board prep sessions), but you check the meeting notes doc. The notes show a section titled "Product Org Updates" with bullet points about the platform reorg and team consolidation. No mention of Marcus's promotion. You check Slack and find the #elt-team channel from June 18. Jamie posted: "Quick update: proposing to move Marcus Thompson to Director level as part of the reorg, he'll own platform product strategy. Supportive?" Three reactions: thumbs up from VP Sales, eyes emoji from CFO, and no reaction from CEO. No written responses.

You also find a 1:1 note between Jamie and the CEO from June 10 (you have view access to their shared 1:1 doc). Jamie's agenda item: "Marcus promotion - want to move him to Director." James's note in response: "Love Marcus but two-level jump is aggressive. Can we do Senior → Group PM first? Also need to staff up the Group PM layer per our flattening goals." Jamie's reply note: "Will think about structure."

HR sent you a Slack DM yesterday: "Marcus promotion packet is complete pending your CoS sign-off. Comp Committee meets Friday and we need CEO confirmation since it's skip-level. Can you verify?"

You notice the promotion effective date is listed as July 1 (4 days away) and Marcus has already been added to the "Product Leadership" Slack channel as of June 22.
question: What is the correct approval status for Marcus Thompson's skip-level promotion to Director?

contributor.name: Amanda Liu
contributor.title: Chief of Staff to the CEO
contributor.domain_expertise: Executive decision tracking, informal approval channels, reorg execution

choices: Approved with Comp Committee contingency - The ELT Slack reactions constitute sufficient executive consensus, but must go to Comp Committee before July 1 effective date due to $195K base
Denied - The January 2026 policy requires explicit CEO approval for skip-level promotions and Slack reactions do not constitute documented approval for a promotion of this magnitude
Incomplete approval chain - CEO expressed concerns about two-level jump in June 10 1:1 and requested Group PM intermediate step; no documented reversal of that guidance exists
Approved - CEO gave verbal approval in the June 18 ELT meeting as documented in the promotion packet, and the reorg context justifies the skip-level structure
